html:
The royal pyramids of the kingdom of Kush, built in what is now northern Sudan from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE. Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt, about two hundred of them.

The first was built for Piye at el-Kurru, near Napata, after he conquered Egypt. Kushite kings had seen the much older pyramids of Egypt and revived the idea for themselves, centuries after Egypt had stopped building them. His successor Taharqa began a new royal cemetery at Nuri, with the largest pyramid of all.

When the capital moved south to Meroë, around 300 BCE, kings and queens were buried there.

Nubian pyramids look different from the Egyptian ones at Giza. They are much smaller and their sides are much steeper. The burial chamber lies in the rock beneath, and a small chapel with carved walls stands against the east face.

Many were damaged in the 1830s by the Italian treasure hunter Giuseppe Ferlini, who knocked the tops off dozens looking for gold. The pyramids of Meroë became a World Heritage Site in 2011.
